options.label: Aspect ratio
options.description: Keep the console's own picture shape, or stretch it to fill the screen.

options.label: Integer scaling
options.description: Only enlarge the picture by whole steps, so every pixel has the same size. Leaves borders around it.

options.label: Screen filter
options.description: Sharp keeps crisp square pixels; Smooth blurs them slightly when the picture is enlarged.

options.label: VSync
options.description: Wait for the screen between frames: no tearing. Off paces the game by its sound instead.

options.label: Show frame rate
options.description: armGBA draws the frames per second in a corner of the screen.

notes: frontend.cfg is armGBA's own settings file: `key = value` lines, no sections (the launcher and these options address the root, section ""); # starts a comment. Read by settingsRead -> takeSetting (frontend/settings.c), written whole by settingsWrite whenever the menu changes a setting and on quit: unknown keys are dropped, known ones kept. Booleans are the words true/false (anything but "true" reads as false); strings may be quoted.

stretch (Stretch to fill, default false) and integer_scale (default false) size the picture in the window (frontend/main.c: applyWindowSize/present); filter is enum Filter: 0 FILTER_SHARP (nearest), 1 FILTER_SMOOTH (linear) via SDL_HINT_RENDER_SCALE_QUALITY; vsync (default true) is the renderer's VSync and the frame pacing (with it off the game is paced by the audio queue, settings.latency); show_fps (default false) draws the frame rate on screen (ACT_FPS toggles the same setting).

Left out: renderer (SDL_Renderer picks the GPU backend itself; no setting), resolution and widescreen_hack (no such setting for GB/GBA), frameskip (none). The LCD grid, ghosting and Game Boy screen palettes are core options in ~/.config/armgba/armgba.cfg (armgba_lcd_grid, armgba_lcd_ghosting, armgba_gb_screen...; frontend/settings.c optionsWrite), reachable in armGBA's own Core tab; a RetroForge option for them can come with the shader phase.
